about.text: Cheese whose curd has part of its whey drawn off and replaced with water while it is being made, diluting its milk sugar so that less lactic acid forms: the cheese ends up less acidic and smooth in texture. Gouda, Edam, Havarti and Tilsiter are made this way.

how.text: Replacing whey with water washes out lactose, so less lactic acid forms later and the cheese avoids a sour, brittle texture. This gives the smooth, supple body of Gouda- and Havarti-type cheeses.
